subject.title: wiki_status leaks the existence of another agent's bridged memory artifacts via an unscoped count

question: Should memory-wiki status and doctor counts be agent-scoped for all callers, or should operator CLI/Gateway diagnostics retain an explicitly global view while agent-visible tools are scoped?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the permanent security boundary differs between agent-visible tools and operator diagnostics; automation should not choose that contract silently.

options.title: Scope agent tools and explicit global diagnostics
options.body: Thread caller/default agent scope into agent-visible status, and keep a clearly labeled or explicitly selected operator-global view for CLI/Gateway diagnostics.

options.title: Scope every status surface by default
options.body: Filter all status and doctor counts by a default or requested agent, favoring the strictest privacy default over existing operator diagnostics behavior.

options.title: Consolidate with content-disclosure repair
options.body: Fix this existence leak in the same security PR as the sibling full-content leak, with status-specific tests so this surface is not missed.

recommendation.title: Scope agent tools and explicit global diagnostics
recommendation.body: Thread caller/default agent scope into agent-visible status, and keep a clearly labeled or explicitly selected operator-global view for CLI/Gateway diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: The bridge/status behavior traces most directly to vincentkoc's feature-history commits, so they are the best available owner for the boundary decision.
